Hi Jordan 	6

Thanks again for the call earlier 	6 really appreciate the context on your volume and quality targets. Quick recap and next steps based on what we discussed: 

- Goals you shared: replace existing hosted LLM with lower cost-per-token while keeping pass-rate on the classification prompts >= 95% and 99th latency < 300ms for interactive flows.
- Recommended models to evaluate (based on your accuracy/latency tradeoff):
  - redwood-llm-4k-q8 (recommended starting point) 	6 strong latency profile for 2k context and good tuning stability
  - open-super-13b-8bit (for higher raw-quality baseline; slightly higher cost)

Attachments: acme_benchmark_summary.pdf (quick read), prompt-set_v1.csv (the evaluation prompts we used). Also attaching our Redwood-verified performance profiles (redwood_verified_profiles.json) for the model variants we ran.

Key Redwood-verified numbers from the initial runs (single-GPU, warm cache):
- redwood-llm-4k-q8: throughput ~300 TPS (short contexts), p50 token latency ~45ms, p95 ~130ms, p99 ~220ms (@ 64-token response bucket). At 2k context these shift: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~350ms.
- open-super-13b-8bit: throughput ~120 TPS, p50 token latency ~110ms, p95 ~300ms.

Notes:
- All numbers are for the benchmark harness linked below and will vary by prompt mix; the attached JSON has the full percentile distributions.
- We saw a small quality regression on one classification prompt when switching from fp16 -> q8 quantization; we flagged it in the summary. We typically run targeted prompt-level evals and can do a regression analysis on your exact prompt set.

Links: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-dynamics/summary (dashboard with full run), drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-prompt-set

Next steps I propose:
1) If helpful, we can provision a 5-day eval workspace that runs the benchmark with your full prompt set and gives a side-by-side of accuracy and latency.
2) Tech deep-dive with Alex to validate p95/p99 numbers at 2k context and to discuss caching/warm-start behavior.
3) If results look good, we can push a scoped dedicated trial (reserved capacity) and discuss pricing/commit.

Would you be available for a 30-min technical deep-dive next Tuesday (Apr 7) at 10am PT? If yes I can loop in our SRE for throughput sizing.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Hi Jordan 	6

Quick answers to your questions: 

1) 2k context latency (verified):
   - redwood-llm-4k-q8: p95 ~360ms, p99 ~520ms (these are token-level percentiles observed in our harness with mixed prompt lengths; full distribution in redwood_verified_profiles.json).
   - open-super-13b-8bit: p95 ~420ms, p99 ~700ms.

2) Quality regressions post-quantization:
   - Frequency: small regressions (1-3% drop on a targeted prompt) are uncommon across wide prompt sets but possible on edge prompts. In our experience with similar customers, regressions are concentrated on short, brittle prompts that rely on exact tokenization artifacts.
   - Mitigations: 1) run targeted prompt-level A/B evaluation (we can do this on your prompt-set_v1.csv), 2) try intermediate quantization (q8+per-channel calibration) or keep critical prompts routed to fp16/8bit hybrid config, 3) prompt-engineer small anchors to stabilize outputs. We can automate per-prompt routing in Redwood (rules-based routing by prompt signature).

3) Eval workspace options:
   - Hosted Redwood eval (fastest): runs on our hosted infra; we can mask PII by default and provide isolated project workspaces.
   - Private eval (recommended for PII): we can run the harness inside your VPC via Redwood Private for a time-boxed evaluation. Procurement typically prefers this for regulated data and we can provide SOC2 docs.

I also linked the exact benchmark run for the numbers above: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-dynamics/summary

If you want, we can spin up the private eval for 72 hours and run a full regression sweep across prompt-set_v1.csv. That will give you per-prompt pass/fail and a suggested routing config (keep/quantize/fallback).

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
